presentation.label: SINGLE-HEAD ECHO
presentation.summary: A single-head echo with wow, flutter and tape age.
presentation.overview: A single-head tape echo with wow, randomized flutter and tape age. Explore drifting repeats, worn tape texture and feedback, with free or beat-synced timing.
usage: Choose TAPE ECHO in FX2. SYNC selects FREE timing or BEAT divisions; TIME adjusts the delay.

FDBK controls repeats, WOW adds pitch movement and flutter, and AGE changes bandwidth and tape noise. MIX sets the balance: up to 64 the echo rises to full level over the whole dry signal, then the dry fades out to the echo alone at 127.
When migrating older projects, former HEADS locks now address AGE. Back up projects and review old effect defaults and parameter locks.

controls.name: TIME
controls.doc: FREE: 46..231 ms; BEAT: twelve note divisions from 1/64 to dotted 1/4

controls.name: FDBK
controls.doc: repeat intensity; the upper range safely self-oscillates from tape noise

controls.name: WOW
controls.doc: 0.8 Hz wow plus irregular flutter; about 8 cents at 44, 22 cents at 127

controls.name: AGE
controls.doc: repeat bandwidth, flutter and noise; fresh at 0, worn at 127

controls.name: SYNC
controls.doc: FREE uses milliseconds; BEAT quantises TIME from stock tempo

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: 0 is exact dry; up to 64 the echo rises to full level over the whole dry signal, then the dry fades out, leaving the echo alone at 127

limitations: The pinned hardware record reports six instances running and a seventh freezing the unit; that limit remains open. Recorded gates cover native arithmetic parity, dirty state, eight-instance stress, moving controls and repeat/feedback behavior. Hardware timing and worst-case CPU headroom remain unqualified. From 0.1.8 every instance holds for one block when stock's delay routine starts more than a quarter frame late; that hold is not yet observed on a unit. 0.1.9 needs base 0.8's two-argument ev_frame_deadline: it also holds a block that would end past the frame's deadline (a held block plays its dry signal at the level MIX gives it and its own input recorded to the tape through the record path, without the repeat the feedback would have added), and passes every instance dry at MIX's dry level while the base rests it on a pattern past the frame ceiling, starting the tape afresh after; none of this is observed on a unit yet.

storage.label: CPU state / shared arena
storage.conditions: 1,600 bytes for eight tracks. Uses the shared 10 MiB DRAM platform reservation and existing stock delay rings; these are not additive per module. No DSP delay buffer.

processing.label: CPU instruction peak
processing.conditions: Eight instances with all controls reversing in BEAT mode (22,571 in 0.1.7). FREE peaked at 19,178. One instance on the default page costs 1,800 instructions a frame (2,075 in 0.1.7); eight settled instances 14,315 for the whole routine (15,283). These emulator instruction counts are not hardware cycles or CPU percentages.

impact.conditions: Audio modules are rated for an active instance, including expensive modes and changing controls; MIDI/USB features are rated while enabled. More tracks or instances increase demand. Shared runtime reservations and reused stock buffers are not added again per module. These rough source-backed tiers do not establish hardware headroom or qualification.

cpu.rationale: Tape Echo processes audio continuously on ColdFire. Eight modulated instances peak at 22,586 emulator instructions per frame in BEAT mode, versus 7,628 for eight stock DELAY instances in the same record. High is a relative work estimate, not a CPU percentage.

dsp.rationale: The DSP side is the documented empty passthrough with one NOP per sample and no tape delay buffer. This indicates minimal added DSP demand while CPU processing carries the effect.

memory.rationale: The module adds 200 bytes of state per track plus code and coefficient tables, while reusing stock delay rings. The common 10 MiB DRAM platform arena is shared rather than additive per instance. Moderate is an incremental footprint estimate.

cpuPrice.conditions: MKII, the owner's project Tresor Prep bank A pattern A01 Part 1 playing at 138 BPM (four-on-the-floor kick on T1, sample tracks sounding on T2, T5 and T6); FX1/FX2 before the module: T1 FILTER/NONE, T2 FILTER/DELAY, T3-T4 CHORUS/NONE, T5-T8 FILTER/DELAY; the effect measured on T1 FX2 in place of NONE; base development twin d3d71297 of base 0.7.8 (main 02dfa20ca); 8 s per reading. Frame interrupt 41 % before, 41.4 % installed and used nowhere, 48.7 % on T1 FX2; CPU meter 60.3 % before, 60.3 % at rest, 70.3 % in use.

tests.summary: 0.1.9 subscribes to base 0.8's ev_frame_deadline: a block that would end past the frame's deadline is held (its dry signal at the level MIX gives it and its own input recorded to the tape through the record path, without the repeat the feedback would have added), and while the base rests Tape Echo on a pattern past the frame ceiling every instance passes the dry signal at MIX's dry level with no echo, tail or ring write, its tape starting afresh after. Its echo arithmetic is 0.1.8's; on the emulator the hold, the rest and the wake keep the dry level within 1 LSB of the full path's at MIX 32, 64, 96 and 127; on the owner's MKII (base 0.8 twin, 23 November 2026) the overload scene's frame-interrupt share fell from 69.0 % with 0.1.6 to 55.6 %, while one to three instances in ordinary use measured dearer than 0.1.6; not listened to on a unit yet. 0.1.8 produces the same samples as 0.1.7 with less ColdFire work: other effects' tracks leave its hook in assembly, steady blocks skip the control half, and the per-track entry is assembly. One instance on the default page executes 1,800 instructions a frame against 2,075. A new overload hold drops one block of echo when stock's delay routine starts more than a quarter frame late. The ColdFire kernels and the steady path match their native oracle bit for bit on the emulator; nothing is measured on a unit yet. The pinned hardware record reports six instances running and a seventh freezing the unit; that limit remains open. See TESTING.md.

access.location: Audio track FX2 SETUP: Tape Echo in the effect chooser.
steps: Select an audio track with its TRACK key.
Hold FUNC and press FX2 to open FX2 SETUP.
Turn LEVEL to Tape Echo and press YES to assign it.
Press FX2 to close SETUP, then adjust TIME, FDBK, WOW, AGE, SYNC and MIX. All six active controls are on this main page.
